newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: British minister offers "good offices" on Kashmir.
newsitem.headline: British minister offers "good offices" on Kashmir.

text.p: A British Foreign Office minister on Monday offered Britain's help in settling the Kashmir dispute between India and Pakistan, should they want it.

"We are willing to provide our good offices to assist in a negotiated solution, if that were generally thought to be helpful," Derek Fatchett said on a visit to Muzaffarabad, the capital of Pakistani-controlled Azad (free) Kashmir.
Fatchett, the first British minister to visit Pakistan since Britain's new Labour government took power last month, was reiterating a proposal he made on Friday while visiting India.

"The British government will support the search for a just and lasting solution, one that is acceptable to the people of Kashmir, whatever their race or religion," he said at a lunch given by Azad Kashmir Prime Minister Sultan Mehmood.
Fatchett welcomed the revival of talks between India and Pakistan, whose top foreign ministry officials are due to start a new round of negotiations in Islamabad on Thursday.
"The resumption of dialogue between India and Pakistan is an encouraging sign and I hope that there will be meaningful talks on Kashmir and on the issues which divide the two countries...

"Settlement of the Kashmir issue is in the interest of all parties, including India, Pakistan and the Kashmiri people, but the aspirations of the Kashmiri people must be taken into account," the British junior minister declared. Mehmood urged Britain to take an active part in promoting a solution to the conflict over the divided Himalayan region. "We would like to see the new Labour government ( in Britain) play its role to resolve the longstanding Kashmir issue," he said. Fatchett, who arrived in Pakistan on Sunday, also held talks with Ghulam Safi, secretary general of the Azad Kashmir section of the All Party Hurriyat Conference, an umbrella group of political and militant factions opposed to Indian rule.
Safi asked Britain to convene an intra-Kashmiri dialogue to evolve a formula to settle the dispute.
Pakistan has in the past welcomed outside mediation over the Kashmir conflict, which India says must be solved bilaterally.
The two countries have fought two of their three wars since independence from Britain 50 years ago over Kashmir.
